Given that $\angle BED + \angle C = 90^\circ$ and $\triangle BED$ is symmetrical to $\triangle FED$ with respect to DE, what is the length of DE?

$\therefore$ $\angle FND=\angle FME=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle B=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral NBEM is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$ $NB=ME$,\\
$\because$ $\angle BED+\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle C+\angle A=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BED=\angle A$,\\
$\because$ $\angle B=\angle B$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BED\sim \triangle BAC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{BD}{BE}=\frac{BC}{BA}=\frac{6}{8}=\frac{3}{4}$,\\
$\because$ Triangle $BED$ and $\triangle FED$ are symmetric with respect to DE,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BED\cong \triangle FED$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DFE=\angle B=90^\circ$, $DF=BD$, $EF=BE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{DF}{EF}=\frac{BD}{BE}=\frac{3}{4}$,\\
$\because$ $\angle FME=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle MEF+\angle MFE=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle MFE+\angle NFD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle MEF=\angle NFD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle NDF\sim \triangle MFE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{NF}{ME}=\frac{DF}{FE}=\frac{3}{4}$,\\
$\therefore$ Let $NF=3x$, $ME=4x$,\\
$\because$ $\angle ANF=\angle B=90^\circ$, $\angle A=\angle A$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ANF\sim \triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{NF}{BC}=\frac{AN}{AB}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{3x}{6}=\frac{8-4x}{8}$,\\
$\therefore$ $x=1$,\\
$\therefore$ $NF=3$, $ME=NB=4$,\\
Let $BD=DF=y$,\\
then $ND=NB-BD=4-y$,\\
